pace.definition: The pace of something is how fast it moves.
pace.sentence: The pace of change has been very, very slow.

pack.definition: When you pack something, you put it in a container to carry with you.
pack.sentence: Did you pack your swimming suit?

package.definition: A package is something in a box, usually to send in the mail.

page.definition: A page is one side of a sheet of paper in a book, newspaper, etc.
page.sentence: The picture of the accident was on page one of the morning's paper.

pain.definition: A strong feeling of hurt or discomfort.
pain.sentence: He was in pain, because his leg was broken.

paint.definition: Paint is a liquid used to colour something.
paint.sentence: Sarah used pink paint to decorate the wall.

pair.definition: A pair is two things that go together.
pair.sentence: She has many pairs of shoes, but she only has one pair of pants.

pale.definition: If someone or something is pale, then their color is very light.

panel.definition: A panel is a flat piece of wood or other material, used as part of a wall or on the side of something.
panel.sentence: The panel made a decision that Paul had won the dance contest.

panic.definition: Panic is a very strong and overwhelming fear which dominates thinking.

paper.definition: Paper is a material for writing and drawing on and is made from wood pulp.
paper.sentence: A notebook is made of sheets of paper.

paragraph.definition: A paragraph is one or more sentences that are written together with no line breaks separating them. Usually they are connected by a single idea.
paragraph.sentence: She knew what it would say after reading the first paragraph.

parallel.definition: When a line is parallel to another line, the two lines do not meet and they are the same distance from each other at every point.
parallel.sentence: The two cars ran parallel to each other.

parent.definition: The parents of a person or animal are its father and mother.
parent.sentence: Children may only enter the pool with a parent or guardian.

park.definition: A park is an outdoor area where people can relax and play.
park.sentence: We sat under the trees and had lunch in Central Park.

part.definition: A part of something is one piece of it or a small amount of it.
part.sentence: As a part of this team, you need to come to practice regularly.

participant.definition: A participant is a person who takes part in something.
participant.sentence: The athlete was a participant at the Olympics.

participate.definition: If you participate in something, you join in it; you take part in something.
participate.sentence: We can both participate in the game.

participation.definition: Participation is the act of joining together with other people to do something.
participation.sentence: After the injury, he was removed from active participation in the war.

particular.definition: A particular thing is the one that you mean and not any other.
particular.sentence: Usually it is not allowed, but in this particular case, it's OK.

particularly.definition: If something is particularly interesting, useful, important, etc., it is more so than usual or more than others.

partly.definition: If something is partly done, only a portion of it is done..

partner.definition: Partners are people, usually two, who are together for a particular purpose, such as for business, sports, or a romantic relationship.
partner.sentence: My partner, Tom, looks after the administrative parts of the business.

partnership.definition: A partnership is two people or groups working together, especially in business.
partnership.sentence: Microsoft has entered into a partnership with Apple to develop software for the Macintosh.

party.definition: A party is when people get together for fun or to celebrate something like a birthday.
party.sentence: The Liberal Party will form the government.

pass.definition: If you pass something, it was ahead of you and you move so that it is now behind you.
pass.sentence: Please, step to the right and let faster people pass on your left.

passage.definition: A passage is the act of passing, from one place to another, or from one state to another.
passage.sentence: Getting a driver's licence is a rite of passage from being a child to becoming an adult.

passenger.definition: A passenger is a person who is riding a vehicle—not the driver.
passenger.sentence: Both passenger trains and freight trains use the same tracks.

passion.definition: Passion is a strong feeling or emotion.
passion.sentence: I have a passion for soap operas!

past.sentence: In the past, many years ago, I was a good doctor.

path.definition: A path is a way to get to a place. It is like a small road, often made of dirt.
path.sentence: That path leads into the woods.

patient.definition: If someone is patient, they can wait without getting upset.
patient.sentence: It's hard to be patient with people who don't listen to you.

pattern.definition: A pattern is a design that uses the same set of elements many times in the same order.
pattern.sentence: The table cloth had a simple pattern of red and white squares.

pause.definition: To pause is to stop current work and do some other work for some time.

pay.definition: If you pay, you give money for something.

payment.definition: A payment is some money that someone is giving to someone else when they're buying something.
payment.sentence: I sent the things they wanted, but I haven't gotten the payment for them yet.

peace.definition: Peace is the way a country is when there is no war.
peace.sentence: The people lived in peace for thirty years.

peak.definition: A peak is a point at the top of an object.

peer.definition: A peer is someone of the same level as you.

pen.definition: A pen is a writing tool that uses ink.
pen.sentence: She sat down with pen and paper and started a letter to her aunt.

penalty.definition: A penalty is a legal punishment for committing a crime.
penalty.sentence: The penalty for his crime was to pay a fine.

pension.definition: A pension is money paid regularly by a government or company to someone who has stopped working, usually because of age or illness.
pension.sentence: When her pension ran out, she had to sell her house and move in with her daughter.

people.definition: The plural form of person; more than one (kind of) person.
people.sentence: Who are these people at the party?

perceive.definition: If you perceive something, you notice it through one of your senses (you see it, touch it, smell it, hear it, or taste it); to be aware of something.
perceive.sentence: He was unable to perceive any difference at all in the room after the changes.

percent.definition: You use percent show the number of parts out of a hundred. The symbol for percent is %.
percent.sentence: The cost of gas has increased seven percent in the last month.

percentage.definition: A percentage of something is the amount as a fraction of 100.

perception.definition: Perception is the action of seeing, hearing, smelling, touching and/or tasting an object that made an impression on the senses.
perception.sentence: The government hopes to change the public's perception of the problem.

perfect.definition: Something that is perfect has no mistakes, problems, or damage.
perfect.sentence: She answered him in perfect Japanese.

perfectly.definition: If something is done perfectly, it is done without mistake.
perfectly.sentence: The car is perfectly aligned in the lot.

perform.definition: When you perform something, you do it.
perform.sentence: Please come help me perform this task.

performance.definition: A performance is a show of acting or music.
performance.sentence: We went to see a performance by local musicians last night.

perhaps.definition: If you say that perhaps something will happen or that perhaps it is true, you mean it may happen or be true.
perhaps.sentence: Perhaps someday I'll learn how to drive.

period.definition: A period is a length of time.
period.sentence: There was a short period when my computer stopped working.

permanent.definition: Permanent means lasting for a long time or forever.
permanent.sentence: His permanent problems cannot be solved.

permission.definition: If you have permission to do something, then the person who has authority over you or over that thing allows you to do it.
permission.sentence: My father gave me permission to go to the city.

permit.definition: If you have a permit to do something, you have a document that says you are allowed to do it, it is legal for you to do it.

person.sentence: She is a very nice person.

personal.definition: If something is personal, that means it is tied to you.

personality.definition: A quality that make a person (or thing) distinct from another.
personality.sentence: My teacher complained to me about my personality.

personally.definition: You say that you, personally, think or feel something, because you want to admit that other people may disagree with you.
personally.sentence: Personally, I feel like I am one of the best workers here.

personnel.definition: Personnel refers to the people who are working for a company and the staff that are working in its office.

perspective.definition: A perspective is a way of looking at or thinking about something.
perspective.sentence: The British media give a completely different perspective from CNN.

persuade.definition: If you persuade somebody to do something, you make them do it, usually by telling them why it's a good thing to do.
persuade.sentence: She tried to persuade her mother to leave Greensburg.

phase.definition: A phase is stage in a process.
phase.sentence: We will look at very basic ideas during the first phase of training.

phenomenon.definition: A phenomenon is a fact or event that you can observe (see or hear or sense), especially one that is not fully understood.
phenomenon.sentence: Football violence is not a particularly new phenomenon, and it isn't only a British problem.

philosophy.definition: Philosophy is the study of the nature of existence and truth: how things are and how they should be.
philosophy.sentence: Plato's writings have been used to teach philosophy, logic, maths, and other subjects.

phone.definition: A phone is a tool for speaking to people who are far away.
phone.sentence: Can I borrow your phone? I need to call my friend.

photo.definition: A photo is a picture created by a camera digitally or on film.
photo.sentence: I took a photo of that beautiful old building.

photograph.definition: A photograph is a picture that is created by a camera digitally or on film.
photograph.sentence: The photograph of the event won a Pulitzer Prize.

phrase.definition: A phrase is a short expression.
phrase.sentence: Sheela liked to use that particular phrase whenever she disagreed with something.

physical.definition: A physical thing or activity is related to the body, or something you can touch.
physical.sentence: The war didn't leave him with any physical injuries, but his mind was badly damaged.

piano.definition: A piano is a large musical instrument that has hammers connected to 88 keys.

pick.definition: When you pick something, you choose it.
pick.sentence: Pick your clothes up off the floor!

picture.definition: A picture is marks on a flat object, like paper, that show shapes, people, or things.
picture.sentence: Mommy, I drew a picture of a cat.

piece.definition: A piece is a part of something that can be or has been separated from it.
piece.sentence: I own a piece of land in the country.

pig.sentence: My sister is such a pig. We bought a bag of sweets and she ate them all in one day.

pile.definition: A pile is a lot of things with some on the bottom and more on top.
pile.sentence: There was a neat pile of sheets and blankets at the foot of each bed.

pilot.definition: A pilot is a person who flies and controls an airplane.
pilot.sentence: I hope the pilot does not crash the plane.

pink.definition: Pink is the color that you get when you mix red and white.

pipe.definition: A tube; a round, hollow piece of metal, plastic, or wood.

pitch.definition: In baseball, a pitch is when the pitcher throws the ball to the batter, who tries to hit it.
pitch.sentence: The batter was going to swing at the pitch but it was too high.

place.definition: A place is a point in space: a town, building, room, or even somewhere on a desk.
place.sentence: It's nice to see the whole family together in one place.

plain.definition: If something is plain, it is clear and easy to see or understand.
plain.sentence: The plain and simple truth was that it was John's fault.

plan.definition: A plan is a clear idea of what you will do, often for a particular goal.
plan.sentence: The school has announced a plan to open two new classrooms.

plane.definition: A plane is a vehicle with wings that flies.
plane.sentence: Can we hurry? I have to catch a plane to Miami.

planet.definition: A planet is one of the 8 bodies that orbit the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

plant.definition: A plant is something that lives and grows in one place. Plants usually have green leaves and roots. Flowers and trees are plants. Plants and animals are the main kinds of life.
plant.sentence: They built a large plant to manufacture automobiles.

plastic.definition: Plastic is a material that can change its shape and is used to pack products.

plate.definition: A plate is a hard flat thing, especially round ones that we put food on.
plate.sentence: He ate everything on his plate.

platform.definition: A platform is a raised stage where speeches, concerts and other performances are made.
platform.sentence: The principal of the school stood on the platform to give a speech to parents about the school's upcoming changes.

play.sentence: Children like to play all day.

player.definition: Someone taking part in a sport or game.
player.sentence: The piano player had long fingers.

pleasant.definition: If something is pleasant, it is enjoyable or agreeable.
pleasant.sentence: When it rains in the summer, it is a pleasant event.

please.definition: We say "please" when we want to ask someone politely to do something.

pleasure.definition: Pleasure is a nice feeling we have when we do something that's fun or that feels good.
pleasure.sentence: Being at this party and seeing my friends again is a real pleasure.

plenty.definition: Plenty of something is a lot of it; more than enough of it.
plenty.sentence: Don't give up straight away darling. You've still got plenty of time to go yet.

plot.definition: A plot is the course of a story. It is the main things that happen in a story.
plot.sentence: They concocted a plot to discredit the governor.

plus.definition: A plus is a good thing.
plus.sentence: On the plus side though, it is small and easy to use.

pocket.definition: A pocket is a small empty space, usually in your clothes, usually to carry things in.
pocket.sentence: I usually put my keys in my pants' pocket, but I can't find them now.

poem.definition: A composition written in metrical feet forming rhythmical lines.

poet.definition: A poet is someone who creates poetry. If you write poems you are being a poet.

poetry.sentence: Poetry is much cheaper than painting since you don't need special supplies.

point.definition: A point is a position with no size, or a small dot.
point.sentence: These two lines meet at this point.

police.definition: The police are the government force who enforce laws, prevent crime, stop and arrest criminals, regulate traffic, help maintain public order, and help with emergencies.
police.sentence: When we saw the man take the money, we called the police.

policy.definition: A policy is an official rule or idea that explain how to act in certain situations.
policy.sentence: The government is suggesting a significant change in economic policy.

political.definition: Something is political if it is related to politics.
political.sentence: He supports the Democratic political party.

politician.definition: A politician is a person who is involved in politics, especially those in elected offices.

politics.definition: Politics is the activity of controlling, affecting or studying an organisation, especially a government.
politics.sentence: The Prime Minister entered politics when she was in university.

poll.definition: A poll is a process of asking people for their opinions about something and counting the results.
poll.sentence: Senator McCain continues to hold a two-point lead in the daily tracking poll.

pollution.definition: Pollution is when bad or harmful things are put into the environment.
pollution.sentence: Nobody visits the river any more because of all the pollution.

pool.definition: A pool is hole that holds water. Usually, it is for people to swim in.
pool.sentence: Our hotel had a large indoor pool.

poor.definition: Someone who is poor has little or no money.

pop.definition: A loud sound, like a cork coming out of a bottle.
pop.sentence: Coca-cola is my favorite brand of pop.

popular.definition: If something is popular many people like, love, or enjoy it.
popular.sentence: Beth is one of the popular girls in my class.

population.definition: The population of a place is the people or animals that live there.
population.sentence: The population of a city is higher than that of a town.

port.definition: A port is a place for ships to stop to trade or refuel.

portion.definition: A portion is a part of something.
portion.sentence: We need to put more signs up in this portion of the city.

portrait.definition: A portrait is a painting or picture of a person's head and shoulders.
portrait.sentence: The portrait of the former queen sold for several million dollars.

pose.sentence: What kind of pose is best for this photograph?

position.definition: The position of something is the place where the thing is.
position.sentence: The position of the table is two metres from the wall.

positive.definition: If something is positive, it is good, happy, or wanted.
positive.sentence: A balanced diet, exercise, and a positive attitude are all things that give you a sense of well being.

possess.sentence: He does not possess a car.

possession.definition: Power or control over something, as distinct from lawful ownership; holding or occupancy.
possession.sentence: I have possession of some valuable antiques.

possibility.definition: If there is a possibility of something, it might happen or it might be true.
possibility.sentence: There is a real possibility of war.

possible.definition: If something is possible, it is able to be done; doable; not impossible.
possible.sentence: Life on other planets is possible.

possibly.definition: You use possibly to say that something might be true.
possibly.sentence: This is possibly the biggest tree in the city.

post.definition: Post is the letters and parcels that you send to other people.
post.sentence: There's no post today because it's a Sunday.

pot.definition: A metal container for cooking. People can cook food by putting the food in a pot and putting the pot on a stove.

potato.definition: A potato is a food that grows under the ground, which is round and white inside.

potential.definition: A potential customer, benefit, problem, etc. is one that might happen in the future.
potential.sentence: Realistic goals can then be set to prevent potential problems from becoming actual ones.

potentially.definition: If something has a chance of potentially happening, there is a chance for it to happen.

pound.definition: A pound is a unit of currency used in Britain.
pound.sentence: Unlicensed dogs will be taken to the pound.

pour.definition: If you pour something, you let it flow from one place to another.

poverty.definition: Poverty is the condition of being poor.

power.definition: Strength, energy, force, control. A quality that can make things happen.
power.sentence: His muscles have a lot of power.

powerful.definition: If someone (or something) is powerful, they have much power.
powerful.sentence: The king is a very powerful man.

practical.definition: If something is practical, it works and is not more difficult that it should be. It makes sense and is good for real life.
practical.sentence: He is a very practical person.

practice.definition: If you practice something, you do it again and again to improve your ability.
practice.sentence: The class was going to practice writing skills for homework.

praise.definition: If you praise someone, then you say good things about them.
praise.sentence: We will praise him for his brave deed.

pray.definition: If you pray, you make a wish or give thanks to a god believing they will pay attention or make the wish come true.
pray.sentence: I decided to pray. I prayed for somebody to help me.

precise.definition: If something is precise it is correct and exact.
precise.sentence: Young children are often unable to give a precise definition for words they know very well.

precisely.definition: When something happens precisely, it happens in an exact and precise manner.
precisely.sentence: The egg flew out the window and landed precisely on Mr. Norton's bald head.

predict.definition: If you predict something, you say that it will happen before anyone observes it.
predict.sentence: It is still difficult to accurately predict the weather more than two days in advance.

prefer.definition: If you prefer something, you like it more than another thing.
prefer.sentence: Sometimes I eat in restaurants, but I prefer to cook.

preference.definition: A preference is something that you like more than others.
preference.sentence: My own preference is for good literature.

pregnancy.definition: A pregnancy when a female is pregnant.
pregnancy.sentence: She was in the third month of her pregnancy.

pregnant.definition: If a female is pregnant, she has a baby growing inside her.
pregnant.sentence: At that time, she was already eight months pregnant with their son, Bradley.

premise.definition: A premise is a set of ideas from which you can put forward an answer or reach conclusion.
premise.sentence: A basic premise of Christianity is to treat other people like you want to be treated.

preparation.definition: Preparation is the act of preparing or getting something ready.
preparation.sentence: In preparation for the event, each person chipped in and bought a gift.

prepare.definition: When we prepare something, we get it ready.
prepare.sentence: We must hope for the best and prepare for the worst.

presence.definition: An instance of being around – being near, in sight.
presence.sentence: He tested for the presence of radon.

present.definition: A present is a gift; something that someone gives to someone else.
present.sentence: Here's a birthday present for you. I hope you like it.

presentation.definition: To show or speak in public about something, usually done in a formal way.
presentation.sentence: The professor gave a presentation to a group of doctors on the benefits of universal healthcare.

preserve.definition: A hunting preserve is an area of land where hunting is allowed.
preserve.sentence: Medicine is no longer a male preserve.

president.definition: A president is the person in charge of a country.

presidential.sentence: Dan Quayle didn't appear very presidential.

press.definition: The press are the people and organisations that report the news.
press.sentence: The president gave an interview with members of the press.

pressure.definition: In science, pressure is force applied over an area.
pressure.sentence: It hurt when the doctor put pressure on her cut foot.

presumably.definition: You use presumably to show that you expect or believe something to be true, but you don't know.
presumably.sentence: The disease presumably originated in Canada.

pretend.definition: If you pretend that something is true, you play that it is true but you know that it is not.
pretend.sentence: I'll be quiet. Just pretend I'm not here.

pretty.definition: You use pretty before an adjective or adverb to mean "more than a little".
pretty.sentence: She was pretty sure that he'd say yes.

prevent.definition: When you prevent something, you stop it from happening.
prevent.sentence: To prevent accidents, you must do everything with care.

previous.definition: If something happened at a previous time, it happened before a particular time.
previous.sentence: Last year, we lived in Seoul, but the previous year we were in Moscow.

previously.definition: If something was done previously, it was done before.
previously.sentence: We discovered a language that was previously unknown.

price.definition: The amount of money you need to pay to buy something.
price.sentence: The price of this book is ten dollars.

pride.definition: Pride is the state of being proud.
pride.sentence: He takes pride in his son's success.

primarily.sentence: This is primarily a question of economics.

primary.sentence: Most patients are managed in primary care but the vast majority of research publications derive from hospitals.

prime.definition: If something is prime, it is best, most important, most suitable, or in some way number one.
prime.sentence: Canada is a prime example of a multicultural country.

principal.definition: The principal thing is the main or most important one.
principal.sentence: Canada's principal trading partner is the USA.

principle.definition: Principles are personal rules that tell you what is right and wrong.
principle.sentence: One principle I follow is not to have regret.

print.definition: If you print a picture, book, newspaper, etc., you make a copy of it on paper with a machine using ink or toner.
print.sentence: Can you print off a copy for me so I can read it on the train?

printer.sentence: I used the printer to make a copy of my project.

prior.sentence: We learned that police had prior knowledge of the attack.

priority.definition: A priority is something that is important; you want to do it first or spend more time or money on it than other things.
priority.sentence: Learning the language is a high priority for all people who move to the country.

prison.definition: A place for people who break the law.

prisoner.definition: A prisoner is a person imprisoned, while on trial or serving a sentence.
prisoner.sentence: He kept his mother as a prisoner in her bedroom until she agreed to change her will.

private.definition: Private is for only one person or a small number of people to see or know.
private.sentence: I don't want to tell you how much money I have; that's private.

privilege.definition: A privilege is a certain thing that someone is allowed to do or have. That is, not everyone is allowed to do or have it.
privilege.sentence: Being able to drive is a privilege not a right.

prize.definition: A prize is something that you receive for winning or doing well.
prize.sentence: She was the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

pro.definition: A pro is somebody who is very good at what they do; short for professional.
pro.sentence: She's real pro who cares about her job.

probability.sentence: I took a class in probability and statistics.

probably.definition: If something is probably true, or will probably happen, it means there is a high chance of it.
probably.sentence: I'm not sure what I'm doing tonight, but I'll probably stay home and study.

problem.definition: A problem is something that is difficult to do, understand, or believe.
problem.sentence: You should see your doctor if you think you have a health problem.

procedure.definition: A procedure is a particular way of doing something.
procedure.sentence: Because police did not follow procedure, the criminal was set free.

proceed.definition: When you proceed, you go forward with something.

process.definition: A process is a series of steps that you take for a particular purpose.
process.sentence: Let us look at the factors considered during the formal decision-making process.

produce.definition: Someone or something produces something when they make it or create it or make it come out.
produce.sentence: The tree would not produce fruit.

producer.definition: Producer is one who participates in creating of goods and services for money.
producer.sentence: Maine is a leading producer of potatoes.

product.definition: A product is an item that can be bought.
product.sentence: They improve their product every year.

production.definition: Production is when something is produced.
production.sentence: The machine is being used for production now.

profession.definition: A profession is a job that needs special skills, such as a doctor.
profession.sentence: Teaching is often considered a noble profession.

professional.definition: About a job such as doctor, lawyer, accountant, etc.
professional.sentence: The group offers free professional advice on legal matters and housing.

professor.definition: A professor is a teacher at a college or university.

profile.definition: A profile is a short biographical description of a person.

profit.definition: A profit is money made that is over the total amount spent on the thing being sold.

program.definition: When you program a computer, you use code to tell the computer what to do.
program.sentence: The student can program the computer to calculate all of his statistics.

progress.definition: Progress is moving forward or getting better (more good).
progress.sentence: We didn't make much progress on the road, only a mile.

project.definition: A project is a complex job or assignment, often involving research or construction.
project.sentence: She's a project manager with British construction company John Mowlem.

promise.definition: When someone is making a promise to a person, he is saying what he plans to do for that person.
promise.sentence: Jane was angry that John broke his promise to take her out to the movies.

promote.definition: If you promote someone or something, you help it to get bigger, higher, or more popular.

promotion.definition: If you get a promotion you move up in rank or position.
promotion.sentence: He received a promotion to sergeant.

prompt.definition: If something or someone is prompt, then they are very quick.
prompt.sentence: He was very prompt at getting a new job.

proof.definition: Proof is evidence which shows something is correct.
proof.sentence: He has proof that he was not at the crime scene. A witness says that they were somewhere else.

proper.definition: The proper way, place, use, etc. is the right one.
proper.sentence: What is the proper way to write a letter?

properly.definition: If you do something properly, you do it in the right way.
properly.sentence: We need to make sure that police are properly trained.

property.definition: Property is a thing or things that belong to someone; things that someone owns.
property.sentence: This house is now my property. I've finished paying for it.

proportion.definition: The proportion is the relationship in size between one part and another.
proportion.sentence: Health care spending is taking up a much larger proportion of the government budget.

proposal.definition: A proposal is something that someone suggests doing.

propose.definition: When you propose something, you say that it should be done or chosen, usually in a formal situation.
propose.sentence: I would like to propose that the problems we have had are actually not because of money.

prospect.definition: A prospect is what you think will happen in the future.
prospect.sentence: There's a good prospect of this building being converted into a school.

protect.definition: If you protect something or someone, you keep it safe; you stop it from being harmed.

protection.definition: Protection is keeping something or someone safe.
protection.sentence: She ran away from her abusive husband to her brother for protection.

protein.definition: Protein is a natural substances in food such as meat, milk, and beans.
protein.sentence: Dr. Lecter told me that if I ate more protein, it would help me get bigger and stronger.

protest.definition: Someone protests something when they say loudly or strongly that the thing is bad.
protest.sentence: The people walked in the street holding signs to protest the war.

proud.definition: If you are proud of or about something you have done, you feel good about it.
proud.sentence: I feel proud that we fought in the war, even if most people think we should have stayed home.

prove.definition: When you prove something, you demonstrate that it is for real and true.
prove.sentence: I will prove my method is more effective than yours.

provide.definition: When you provide something, you make it available.

province.definition: A province is a major subdivision of a country.
province.sentence: It was his province to take care of himself.

provision.definition: A provision is an item that is kept by a person that he needs to support himself for the future.
provision.sentence: He kept a provision of food with him for the trip.

psychological.sentence: We are concerned about the psychological effect the experience may have on the girls.

public.definition: Something is public if it is about or for all the people.
public.sentence: You can't tell me to go away. This is a public place.

publication.definition: Publication is the act of making a book or other thing publicly known or available where the public can use it.
publication.sentence: The Report itself and the debate that followed its publication have been useful.

publisher.definition: A publisher is a person or a company that prints books, magazines, etc. and sells them to people.

pull.definition: Someone pulls something when they use their hands to move the thing closer to themselves.
pull.sentence: Pull the handle if you want to open the door.

pump.definition: To make water or any other liquid move using a machine.

pupil.definition: A pupil is a student, especially a young one.

purchase.definition: If you purchase something, you buy it.

pure.definition: If something is pure, it is not dirty or covered by anything that makes it unclean.

purpose.definition: A purpose is reason for doing something or for existing.
purpose.sentence: The main purpose of the visit was to see the new building.

pursue.definition: If you pursue a job or hobby, you do it for a long time.
pursue.sentence: The band motivated her to pursue a career in music.

push.definition: If you push something, you touch it with a force away from your body.
push.sentence: You have to push that door quite hard before it will open.

put.definition: When you put a thing someplace, you move a thing to a place.
put.sentence: I always put my books on the table when I get home from school.
